description: A small leathery wing, torn at the trailing edge. Something flies on these; nobody has cornered it yet.
lore: Buyers want a pair. They always want a pair — one wing is an accident, two are a specimen — and in all the years of the trade not one honest pair has come in off the same creature. So the trade makes them. Take a big wing and a small one, trim the big one's trailing edge until the shapes agree, then rough the cut with a thumbnail so it reads as a tear. That is why so many torn wings are torn so tidily, and why a careful buyer holds the two edges up together and hunts for the same nick in both. Ten gold each, twenty-eight the pair, which tells you what the lie is worth. The whole point of [[lore/the_hard_pieces|a pile of leavings]] is that the details are still attached to it. This is the trade filing them off for eight gold, and the men who do it will tell you they are only giving people what they came in for.
gm_notes: Faked pairs are the standard fraud in junk; the trimmed trailing edge is the tell, and it invalidates a lot of evidence in circulation. Comic until you count what it costs the record.
